title: Where the number of orders comes from: caps, prices, conservation and one fill
claim: S1: lambda never decreases. S2: the corner rule across crossing splits keeps every relation of splits, hence k and lambda. S3: a cap of d orders refills from a full d-grid. S4: the corner knot set is always a fill; along a chain of a full grid it raises lambda by exactly one; Q_d has no fill. S5: a greedy price on states and orders raises at a full non-cube grid iff its increment is below two states, so the number is written into the price. S6: one fill on a line makes exactly two orders; the keep rule never fills a line. S7: after its first fill the seed-and-copy rule keeps a bipartite crossing graph.
standard_statement: Greedy extension of split systems by betweenness constraints: lattice dimension under capped, priced and conservative rules.
